correctness.rationale: The Fano incidence criterion exhausts the pair types. Same-shore pairs have a unique geodesic of length two; a nonincident point and line have exactly the three length-three routes indexed by the lines through the point. Each route must avoid selected internal vertices. A separate shortest-path enumeration tested all 16,384 labelled subsets and recovered (1,14,91,322,651,728,392,58) and 70 size-six plus 58 size-seven facets. One-vertex extension is sufficient by heredity. The 168 Fano collineations and their translates by the part-swapping polarity exhaust the automorphisms because the connected graph has a unique bipartition up to swap. The independent census verified each stated representative and the orbit sizes 28, 42, 2 and 56. Thus the complex is nonpure, with the asserted extrema and totals.
residual_risks: This is an exhaustive certificate for the specified 14-vertex graph only, not an assertion about other projective planes.

evidence: A size enumerator does not by definition record extendibility or the action of Aut(H). The lower number gives only the smallest facet size; the maximum gives only the largest. The equal-size facets here even separate into different orbits.

value.rationale: The Heawood graph is the canonical Fano incidence graph. The exact ordinary visibility complex answers how many configurations extend to optimum and what kinds of maximal obstructions remain: in particular, there are 70 maximal suboptima in two distinct symmetry types, not merely a maximum of seven. The labelled census and full-group reduction are useful as an exact benchmark for visibility-complex and symmetry calculations on incidence graphs.
residual_risks: The contribution is a single natural graph classification; no infinite-family value or historical priority is inferred.
